This is a nonfatal citation overstatement: the original proof already supplies radial motion locally, and the supplier proof also constructs it. F2 now cites only connectedness, and step 1.1 gives the explicit radial homotopy, its boundary compatibility, and the induced homology isomorphism. The surgery presentation and linking-form formula are unchanged.

The exact rejected carrier explicitly says “Let $\widetilde\mu$ be the closed lift of $\mu^q$,” not a closed lift of $\mu$. Its current itemHashJudge equals the rejected tuple hash. The peripheral kernel has basis $(q\mu,\lambda)$, so $\mu^q$ lifts to a primitive closed curve and defines a valid solid-torus meridian slope. Rolfsen Chapter 10.C, printed pp. 297–298, describes this same q-times-covering meridian. No defect or edit is warranted.

The reverse slope matrix and core orientation give minus A inverse, including parallel-copy diagonal pairings, agreeing with Przytycki–Yasuhara Theorem 1.1 and its proof. The forward/reverse-surgery diagram has correct objects, directions and labels. Only F2 and step 1.1, plus its contract mirror, were repaired; the Statement remains byte-identical. This is the repairer’s review, not an independent acceptance.

Checked the complete definition and actual peripheral, exterior-homology and covering-space prerequisite interfaces. Full AC supplies countable choice; the smooth compact exterior meets the local covering hypotheses. The meridian map is surjective, with normal kernel of index q and deck group Z/q. Surjectivity on the boundary gives one torus with lattice generated by mu^q and lambda; mu^q is primitive there. Filling that slope extends by the product local power map with deck rotations and the lifted orientation. The Definition contains no inline hyperlinks and no diagram is needed. Its guard is exactly the assignment before guard; neither item nor metadata was edited.
